question: How is Raymond James positioning itself to recruit advisors away from the wirehouses?

claims.text: On the earnings call published 2025-01-29, Raymond James management said its 'best of both worlds' value proposition combines 'a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture' with the scope of products and capabilities for complex client needs, and that this makes it 'a preferred destination for both current and prospective advisors.'

On the earnings call published 2025-04-23, CEO Paul Shoukry said a change of control at another firm 'always creates a catalyst for advisors to take a look at other options', and that this would 'absolutely increase the opportunities' with advisors seeking the culture and capabilities Raymond James provides. He also said a strong balance sheet 'becomes increasingly important to prospective advisors' seeking strength and stability.

On the earnings call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry contrasted Raymond James with competitors. He said Raymond James attracts advisors 'with our unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check'. He said many competitors 'are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years'. He also said many competitors 'change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products', whereas Raymond James values independence. He added that a stable platform matters amid industry M&A consolidation and disruption.

On the earnings call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said advisors are 'coming from, you know, wires, regionals, other independents'. He said Raymond James has 'the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody', with critical mass and decades of experience in each. He described the draw as the value proposition, cultural fit, platform and multiple affiliation options.

On the call published 2026-01-28, management said its private wealth advisor program and expanded alternative investments platform support advisors who focus on high-net-worth clients. It also cited the newly launched proprietary digital AI operations agent 'Rai'.

On the earnings call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said 'advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities'. He tied this to the firm's strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and 'commitment to independence', and cited more than $1.1 billion in annual technology spend.

On the earnings call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry cited a '97% adviser satisfaction rate' from the firm's surveys. He said Raymond James has 'all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want' and is 'agnostic' about how an adviser affiliates, wanting advisers to 'fall in love with our culture, values and the platform'.

Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) describes AdvisorChoice® as five options: Traditional Employee (book ownership), Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA. The firm's 10-K for the year ended 2025-09-30 also lists RIA and Custody Services as a way advisors affiliate. The Traditional Employee page (as of 2026-05-16) promises 'no quotas, no product pushing' and book ownership.

Trade press (InvestmentNews, published 2026-11-04; indicative only) reports that an Ohio team joining Raymond James cited culture and leadership stability. It describes 'a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026' as advisors at the wirehouse respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.

On the earnings call published 2025-01-29, management said it recruited advisors with approximately $318 million of trailing 12-month production and $51 billion of client assets at their previous firms over the prior 12 months. It said total recruited client assets, including RCS, were nearly $61 billion across all platforms.

On the earnings call published 2025-10-22, management reported fiscal 2025 record recruiting to the domestic independent contractor and employee channels. Trailing 12-month production at previous firms was $407 million, a 21% increase over the prior record. Those advisors had approximately $58 billion of client assets, and total recruited assets including RCS were nearly $63 billion. The firm also reported a record number of financial advisors, 8,943. Shoukry said the pipeline for fiscal 2026 was 'probably the strongest it's ever been entering the fiscal year'.

On the earnings call published 2026-01-28, management reported the first-quarter recruiting result. Trailing 12-month production totaled $96 million and client assets at previous firms were approximately $13 billion. Over the past twelve months, recruited production was nearly $460 million and client assets were over $63 billion. Including RCS, total recruited assets were more than $69 billion. Shoukry said activity was 'broad-based across our affiliation options', 'maybe more heavily tilted in the last six months on the independent contractor side'.

On the earnings call published 2026-04-22 (quarter ended 2026-03-31), management reported recruited production of $141 million and nearly $21 billion of client assets at previous firms. It called this the second highest quarterly result in the firm's history for both recruited production and assets. Management cited 'a robust adviser recruiting pipeline and a strong number of financial advisers who have made commitments to join in the coming quarters'.

On the earnings call published 2026-07-22 (quarter ended 2026-06-30), management reported quarterly recruited production of $156 million and nearly $23 billion of client assets at previous firms. For the first 9 months of the fiscal year, trailing 12-month production totaled $393 million and client assets more than $56 billion. Shoukry said this put the firm 'on a clear path to exceed the record results set in fiscal 2025'. He said the source of recruiting success and the current pipeline 'remains diverse across our affiliation options'.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, published 2026-10-29; indicative only) reports recruited-advisor trailing 12-month production of $538 million for the fiscal year, up from $407 million, representing more than $82 billion in client assets, per Shoukry on the fiscal fourth-quarter call. It says Raymond James no longer reports advisor headcount and had about 8,900 advisors the last time it was broken out.

Trade press (InvestmentNews, published 2026-11-05; indicative only) says Raymond James brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley earlier in 2026 with combined assets exceeding $1 billion. A separate report (published 2026-09-02) describes a UBS team with more than $550 million joining.

The 2025 10-K (period ended 2025-09-30) says independent contractor advisors bear their direct costs and 'receive a higher payout percentage' than employee advisors. On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said much more of the last year's recruiting has come from the independent side, and that the employee side has tiered payouts that rise with production.

Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists headline terms. Traditional Employee requires a minimum of 5 years of experience and offers up to 50% payout. Advisor Select requires a minimum of 3 years and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue, with 70-80% gross payout. Independent Contractor offers 81% to 90% payout, with a minimum T12 of $150,000 to join an existing branch and $400,000 to open a new branch. Corporate RIA offers 81% to 90% payout.

On the call published 2025-10-22, the CFO said fiscal 2025 adjusted compensation expense included amortization of transition assistance for recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors totaling $355 million, up approximately 11% from fiscal 2024.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said the firm broke out retention and transition assistance expense for the first time because recruiting is comparable to 'a pretty decent size acquisition'. He said the firm prefers to recruit one by one because '100% of what we pay in transition assistance is going to retention versus the seller'. On the call published 2026-04-22 he repeated this and said the firm sees 'very good returns' on recruiting.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said 'We have to have a competitive check, but we want the advisors that want to be here over the long term'. He said dialing recruiting spend up or down quarter by quarter yields advisors 'moving or not moving for the highest check'. On the call published 2026-07-22 he said 'we don't lead with the highest check', that 'we have to have competitive economics', and that the firm has 'always been disciplined' on transition assistance.

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says other financial services firms are 'offering guaranteed contracts, upfront payments, and increased compensation'. It also says Raymond James's results may be adversely affected by the costs of loans or other incentives it offers to newly recruited advisors.

On the call published 2025-07-23, Shoukry said 'the environment remains competitive' and that PE-backed roll-ups have been 'extremely aggressive' over the last three years, paying higher multiples. He added that 'in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks', and that the firm was still seeing pressure on its existing advisor base.

On the call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry said 'there are still very rich deals out there from the roll-ups and aggregators'. He said the firm would lose a platform of about $2.7 billion of assets through bank M&A. He said recruiting was 'showing no real signs of slowing down'.

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) names an industry-wide trend of advisors departing traditional firms, including for RIAs backed by private equity. It says this 'has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment'. It also says competition for talent is intense and 'could negatively affect earnings'.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said 'there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups'. He said the advisors Raymond James recruits are not looking for 'a three-five-year destination' with another liquidity event.

On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said catalysts arise 'every 12 to 18 months'. He said private equity and some strategic firms have been competitive, and that he had heard of 'at least 1 or 2 firms that have tried to raise capital' and were unable to. He reported an uptick in commits in the employee affiliation option.

On the call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry said recruiting 'is not something you could turn on and off quarter-to-quarter' and that the firm wants to 'remain consistent'. He said the firm's growth 'remains focused on quality over quantity'. Raymond James describes no pullback in recruiting in these passages.

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, published 2026-10-29; indicative only) quotes Shoukry saying advisors 'don't have to select' a channel and need only assess cultural fit and capabilities. It reports the independent contractor channel is seeing the most interest in dollar volume.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative; it describes channel interest, not compensation or deal terms.

adjacent.text: Raymond James's fiscal 2025 adjusted compensation expense included $355 million of amortization of transition assistance for recruited advisors and retention awards to existing advisors.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

gaps.what: Raymond James: Headline payout ranges are published (company recruiting page, as of 2026-04-21); the full payout grid is not public.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James advisor recruiting materials or recruiter-provided payout grid

gaps.what: Wirehouse-specific deal terms (transition assistance amounts or multiples offered to advisors leaving wirehouses) are not disclosed; only aggregate transition-assistance amortization and general statements are provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James 10-K/10-Q compensation footnotes and investor presentations, or industry recruiter surveys

gaps.what: Raymond James does not break out recruited advisors or assets by source firm type (wirehouse versus regional or independent). Management says only that advisors come from 'wires, regionals, other independents'. Advisor headcount is no longer reported after 8,943 at 2025-09-30.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James earnings call Q&A or investor presentation recruiting slides
